title: Every finite-dimensional point complex has an integral section lattice
statement: Fix D, l and E as in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], with l different from the characteristic, and suppose the specified integral fibre is an equivalence. For each object V of the bounded finite-dimensional E-complex category [def-weil-point-fd-complexes], there is an integral constructible complex K whose specified integral-rational fibre is isomorphic to V. This is an object-existence assertion and contains no Hom comparison or rational functor full-faithfulness assertion.

source.place: Every finite-dimensional point complex has an integral section lattice; extracted from the point-fibre argument; lean/Sheaf/Paper/PointRationalSectionsLattice.lean, pointRationalSectionsLattice

proof.text: For the finitely many nonzero cohomology spaces of V choose finite bases. Lift their vectors to cycles in a representative complex. The zero-differential bounded complex of the corresponding finite free E-spaces maps quasi-isomorphically to that representative. The same finite ranks define a bounded finite free O_E complex P. Completeness of O_E makes P derived complete; its cohomology is finitely generated with finite support. The integral equivalence therefore supplies an integral constructible K with integral sections isomorphic to P. Tensoring with E, and then the specified carrier-size descent counit, identifies its integral-rational fibre with V. Empty support gives the zero complex and the same construction works.

lean.statement:
theorem pointRationalSectionsLattice
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (hi : (pointIntegralFibre D l hl E).IsEquivalence)
    (V : (DerivedCategory.pointFiniteDimensional E).FullSubcategory) :
    ∃ K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E (Spec (.of D.k)),
      Nonempty ((pointIntegralRationalFibre D l hl E).obj K ≅ V)
